subject: Next steps: security intake + processor roster (BrightCare)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Harris <dana.harris@brightcare.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: security intake + processor roster (BrightCare)

Hi Dana — thanks again for the time today. High-level recap and asks so we can keep momentum from the discovery call: 

Call recap:
- BrightCare is evaluating Redwood for document summarization and patient note routing (low-latency inference in prod).
- Main compliance concerns: SOC 2 artifacts, HIPAA / BAA for PHI, and clarity on subprocessors/cloud providers and data flow boundaries.

Asks / next steps we discussed (action owners + suggested target dates):
1) Processor roster: could you share the current list of third-party processors (cloud, analytics, email/SMS providers, monitoring, logging)? Ideally an export or spreadsheet — we can ingest into our vendor map. (Dana / Security) — target: Thu 2026-10-07
2) SOC 2 status: do you have a current SOC 2 Type II report, bridge letter, or timeline to completion? (Dana) — target: 2 weeks
3) HIPAA / PHI handling: confirm whether BrightCare will require Redwood to sign a BAA for the planned scope and whether any PHI will be persistently stored in logs/backups. (Dana) — target: Thu 2026-10-07
4) Data residency & egress constraints: call out any region restrictions or contractual data residency requirements. (Dana) — target: Thu 2026-10-07
5) Security questionnaire: we will kick off our short security intake questionnaire and provide a secure upload link for artifacts (SOC 2, subprocessor roster). We'll CC our security lead and send a link momentarily. (Neha / Redwood) — immediate

I've attached a short Redwood security overview to give your security team quick context (Redwood_Security_Overview.pdf).

If anything above is inaccurate or missing from the call, flag it and I'll update. I will loop in our security point-of-contact (karthik) and legal (marissa) so they can triage artifacts once you upload.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: Redwood_Security_Overview.pdf (summary, stub)

From: Dana Harris <dana.harris@brightcare.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@brightcare.com
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: security intake + processor roster (BrightCare)

Neha — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers and what we'll upload: 

- SOC 2: currently working with our auditor; expecting Type II coverage for core platform controls by Q1 2027. We can provide a bridge letter and summary of control coverage in the meantime.
- HIPAA / PHI: we do process PHI for certain flows. BrightCare requires a signed BAA for any vendor that stores or processes PHI. We need to understand whether Redwood stores PHI in any persistent logs or backups and retention windows for those logs.
- Subprocessors / cloud providers (high level; we'll upload a spreadsheet): AWS (us-east-1) for production, GCP (europe-west1) for analytics pipelines, Twilio for SMS, SendGrid for transactional email, Sentry for error telemetry. We'll upload the full roster (BrightCare_Subprocessors_20260929.xlsx) to the secure link.
- Data residency: production data must remain in us-east-1. Analytics exports to europe-west1 are aggregated and pseudonymized.

We will upload the processor roster and a short SOC attestation document to the link once received. Also attaching a short note asking whether Redwood supports BYOK for encryption keys and how access to logs is audited.

Thanks — Dana
Dana Harris
Senior Security Manager | BrightCare Health
dana.harris@brightcare.com
attachment: BrightCare_Subprocessors_20260929.xlsx (stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Harris <dana.harris@brightcare.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: security intake + processor roster (BrightCare)

Hi Dana — Karthik on Redwood's security team here, thanks for the quick responses. I'm looping Marissa from Legal so we can coordinate on BAA language. 

Actions I'm taking now:
- I've generated a secure questionnaire bundle and upload container for BrightCare: https://security.redwood.ai/sq/BRIGHT-ABC123. Please upload the processor roster (spreadsheet), any SOC attestation/bridge letter, and any architecture diagrams you can share.
- I'm attaching a draft BAA (Redwood_BAA_Draft_v1.docx, stub) for review; Marissa will lead any edits. If BrightCare has a preferred BAA template, please upload that as well.

A few follow-up technical clarifications that help us scope subprocessor risk:
- When you say "production data must remain in us-east-1," do you allow ephemeral inference cache or logs to be routed to our analytics GCP project (europe-west1) if pseudonymized? We can enforce strict routing if required.
- Encryption and keys: we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for stored artifacts on dedicated plans; for hosted API flows we enforce AES-256 at rest and TLS1.2+ in transit. Please indicate which model of deployment you're evaluating (hosted API vs dedicated VPC).
- Access controls & logging: we'll provide an audit log export and show how token-level access is logged. If you have a minimum retention window for audit logs, call that out in the upload.

Suggested timeline to keep this moving:
- Upload roster + SOC artifacts to our secure link by 2026-10-07
- Redwood Security review complete and follow-up Qs by 2026-10-14
- Legal/BAA draft exchange starting 2026-10-11

If helpful, I can propose a 30-minute walkthrough with your security engineering lead to review the roster and any data flow diagrams.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Attachment: Redwood_BAA_Draft_v1.docx (stub)

From: Dana Harris <dana.harris@brightcare.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 18:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: security intake + processor roster (BrightCare)

Karthik — thanks, we'll use the secure upload link and have the roster + attestation uploaded today. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- We'll upload BrightCare_Subprocessors_20260929.xlsx to the link; it includes vendor contract owners and data categories (PHI, PII, aggregated).
- SOC bridge letter: we'll request the auditor to provide a control summary and can share a bridge by mid-Oct.
- BYOK: BrightCare prefers customer-managed keys for production data at rest where possible. If Redwood's hosted API does not support BYOK for the standard plan, please confirm options for Dedicated or Private deployment.
- Retention: our legal team requires a minimum 12 month retention for audit logs; can Redwood produce an export in a common format?

We'll upload the artifacts to https://security.redwood.ai/sq/BRIGHT-ABC123 and ping you once complete. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Dana
Senior Security Manager | BrightCare Health
dana.harris@brightcare.com
